wellsFlip.ciNote: One CI run failed a single unrelated test (pe-property-entitlement.test.ts, a duplicate-key fixture-seeding error in a file this PR never touched) -- confirmed as a pre-existing flake per this repo's own established discipline (RO-ROLE's close set the precedent for exactly this situation), re-ran only the failed job, passed clean on 3503 tests second time.
wellsFlip.criticalFixInThisPR: Every serve-cutover wrapper (wellFactServeCutover.ts and its specialDistricts/cityLimits siblings) called resolveAllowlist(injectedVerdictStore ?? null, ...). Since injectedVerdictStore defaults to undefined outside tests, this ALWAYS passed null in production -- the verdict store was never actually connected, so a slated pair would have silently fallen back to legacy regardless of a real passing gate verdict. Invisible in both PARCEL-B-READER's and PARCEL-B-GATE-SCHED's own closes because the slate shipped empty (the slate-membership check short-circuits before ever reaching the store) -- only became reachable, and only now caught, once a real slate entry existed. Fixed with a shared resolveVerdictStore() helper (parcelGateVerdictRead.ts) that resolves the real env-connected pool (reusing parcel_record_ro's existing connection) when no test override is set.

gateVerdictsActuallyWritten.gap: This card's own CP3 (the live REFUSE search) ran gate-rail-cli.mjs directly and locally -- a read-only evaluation, never the sanctioned Cloud Run job with --apply. Those 18+ checks proved the LIVE DATA state (pass/excluded/refuse) but wrote NOTHING to parcel_gate_verdict. The first post-deploy canary probe (immediately after merging this PR) correctly still showed every county serving legacy -- not a bug in the fix, a genuinely empty verdict table (only 3 pre-existing rows from PARCEL-B-GATE-SCHED's own close: 48055/flood=excluded, 48491/wells=pass, 48491/specialDistricts=pass).

retirement.whatIsActuallyRetired: The SERVE ROUTE no longer calls loadWellFactAtom for any of the 5 slated, gate-passing counties -- proven structurally (wellFactServeCutover.ts's own logic: state !== 'record' is the only branch that reaches loadWellFactAtom) AND live (the production probe above shows sourceAdapter=parcel_record / parcel-record-* refusal codes for all 5 flipped counties, never the legacy atom's own tags, for every parcel checked).
retirement.whatIsHonestlyNotRetired: The underlying well-fact ATOM TABLE and the loadWellFactAtom FUNCTION are not deleted -- both remain live and necessary: (a) Caldwell (48055) still serves from them by design (excluded verdict, stays legacy per this card's own premise 4 until the txgio backfill); (b) they are the allowlist's own fail-closed fallback for every county if the verdict store or gate ever becomes unavailable again. This is a PARTIAL, disclosed retirement -- the route's own call pattern for 5 of 6 counties, not a full decommission of the legacy store. Calling it a full retirement would misrepresent Caldwell's continued, correct dependency on it.
